BUGS TO REPRODUCE + ROOT-CAUSE + FIX (use Playwright against the sandbox with a FAKE IMAP/Mailcow fixture or a local dovecot/greenmail if available; read-only IMAP to the real server is OK for comparing results but NEVER write/flag/move/delete real mail and never send): (1) owner cannot open emails (message view fails/hangs) — find why (getMessage, sanitiser, attachments route, client error handling, hydration, CSP) and make failures visible with retry; (2) company mailboxes contact/admin/support show Santino's mail (e.g. yesterday's list) — mailbox address likely not threaded through list/fetch/cache keys or a stuck client state; (3) images not populating (logo, mailbox avatars) — coordinate: you own avatars in mail; A1 fixes the global asset problem; (4) Sent view looked stale after Refresh — verify cache invalidation/refresh really re-queries IMAP and that sort/pagination is right.

Prefer server-side enforcement that works when the UI is closed: evaluate Mailcow's Rspamd/Sieve (ManageSieve or Mailcow API) vs a worker that applies rules over IMAP on arrival (IDLE/poll) — choose, justify, implement; rules persisted in DB (additive schema) and unit-tested with fixtures; (e) deliverability/mailboxes/templates pages kept functionally intact and polished; (f) general quality-of-life: keyboard shortcuts, bulk select/actions, search, snooze/star persistence if present, error toasts, loading skeletons, mobile layout.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
96	- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
97	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
98	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.
99	
100	## Safety rules
101	
102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
103	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
104	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
105	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
106	- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
107	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
108	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

With routing sorted, my priority shifts to finding actual bugs — I need to dig into MailClient.tsx, ReadingPane, MessageList, FolderRail, and the company mail actions.

For bug 2, I'm tracing how company mailboxes end up showing Santino's mail -- it looks like the stored selected mailbox key in localStorage gets restored on mount when there's no initial active address, causing it to switch into Santino's inbox automatically.

I'm also finding a race condition: the polling logic compares a key against itself (closure variable against the same closure variable), making the staleness check a no-op, so a poll for one mailbox can overwrite the list after the user has already switched to another. There's also no stale-response guard in loadList, so quick mailbox switches can let an old response land after a new one.

That would explain "contact shows Santino's mail" exactly — activeAddress switches but folders/list fail silently and stay stale, possibly from a leftover SSR tab. There's also a concurrency issue: Next.js app router queues server actions sequentially per client, so a slow listMessages call (downloading previews for many messages) could block getMessage from running, which lines up with the "emails won't open" hang, especially with polling and setFlag calls stacking up.

Each message open establishes its own IMAP connection for setFlag and then getMessage, all queued sequentially, and getMessage pulls full message source including large attachments — plus ContactPanel might be triggering its own sender-history search that adds to the queue. I also notice openMessage has no stale-click guard, so rapidly clicking between messages could let an earlier request's result overwrite a newer one.

I should check render.ts for HTML sanitization issues, and look at how ReadingPane renders content — possibly via iframe, where CSP could block srcdoc images. I need to review ReadingPane, ContactPanel, render.ts, MessageList, FolderRail, SenderAvatar, and util to trace this fully.

I realize the sanitizer strips style tags, so CSS-styled emails lose formatting, and inline cid: images never resolve since related attachments are skipped, meaning embedded images won't render. There's also a possible CSP restriction on http: images that could be blocking content — I should check the CSP settings next.

Looking at the MessageBody component, the iframe uses a sandboxed blob URL with allow-same-origin, and since blob documents inherit the CSP of their creating document, the img-src policy would still apply there. I need to check what the CSP actually specifies.

These errors happen once per minute, suggesting a long-lived admin tab left open across a deploy, polling on a 60-second interval and repeatedly calling stale server action IDs that no longer exist in the new deployment, causing every call to fail.

This would explain the "couldn't open message," stale refresh, and mailbox-switch failures all at once -- the tab's UI state updates optimistically while the underlying server actions silently fail, leaving a mismatch between the displayed address and the actual (stale) message list. I want to check lib/chunk-error.ts since it references a confirmed live occurrence right after a promote, and figure out what error shape the client actually receives when a server action ID isn't found so I can build detection logic around it.

The better architectural fix is moving mail data fetches from server actions to route handlers, since those have stable URLs across deploys and avoid the action-queue serialization that's causing hangs. I'm thinking through wrapping the shared mail functions in an API route that both admin and customer products could call via a client-side wrapper, plus adding a version-check endpoint that prompts a reload banner when a new deploy is detected -- then I want to go verify this against the actual chunk-error.ts code and today's attachment route error.

This "Error: Message not found" traces to the getMessage server action on the /admin/inbox page failing because fetchOne returns no message — the owner hit this five times in 13 seconds this morning. I'm considering why fetchOne would fail, starting with the possibility of a wrong mailbox being queried.

My leading suspect is an activeAddress mismatch — a UID from mailbox X getting fetched against mailbox Y, like when the list shows one contact's messages but the active address is set to another, which would explain the mismatch and lines up with bug 2. I'm ruling out folder path issues and the mailbox lock setup since those look fine, so I should pull more log entries to see the frequency and timing of these "Message not found" errors alongside other recent error occurrences.

This "Message not found" error looks like a mailbox mismatch — if the UI is showing Santino's Sent messages (UIDs 200+) but the active address is still set to contact@, fetching that UID against the contact inbox would fail since its UIDs only go up to 83. I'm considering race conditions that could cause this: a stale folder-switch action, a poll response resolving after a mailbox switch completes and overwriting the correct list, or a mount-time restore effect loading the wrong stored address before the switch settles.

Since actions queue sequentially, the poll race likely resolves before the switch's listFolders call, meaning setActiveAddress happens before the next render, so the poll should read the updated address correctly as long as the reassignment lands before the timer fires.

Let me check other possible mismatch sources: the ContactPanel's listMessages path doesn't touch the list, the starred view key looks fine, and SSR fallback for a bad mailbox param just falls back silently to santino without creating a mismatch. Actually, I think I found the real issue: since MailClient stays mounted across client-side navigation between mailbox query params, React reuses the same component instance and ignores new useState initial values from updated props like initialFolders, initialList, and initialActiveAddress — meaning state from the previous mailbox can leak into the new one.

content.thinking:
I'm deciding whether to fork a separate AdminMailClient or build on the shared MailClient component — leaning toward putting the sequencing, mailbox-switch atomicity, and error/retry fixes into the shared client so both admin and customer benefit, while keeping admin-specific features layered on top.

Now I'm questioning whether request serialization or slow preview loading actually explains the "cannot open emails" hang, and estimating that server-side fetch times are too fast to be the real cause. I suspect the real culprit is more likely stale post-deploy action calls silently failing and triggering the "Couldn't open this message" error, rather than a genuine data-fetching bottleneck.

This leads me to a key realization: Server Action IDs in Next 15 are build-dependent hashes, so every deploy breaks any open tab's actions until reload—explaining why opening mail fails, refresh silently fails, and polling silently fails, leaving the UI frozen on stale data. That directly explains the "Sent view stale after Refresh" bug, and likely also explains why switching mailboxes can leave the UI showing the wrong account's data when the switch action itself fails silently.

For the "Message not found" case, it seems plausible the switch wasn't atomic—activeAddress updated before the folder list actually loaded, so a click can race ahead and request a message from the wrong mailbox. The real fix needs the switch to only commit after data loads successfully (reverting on failure), tag each list with its owning mailbox, and have getMessage reference the list's mailbox rather than the global activeAddress.

On the transport side, I'm weighing a dedicated `/api/mail/rpc` route handler for reads and mutations versus sticking with server actions. Server actions already handle origin checks for CSRF, but a custom JSON route would need its own same-origin and content-type checks. Given the complexity of swapping transports for a live product, a simpler middle ground is to keep server actions but add a client-side wrapper that detects stale-deploy errors and prompts a reload.

I'm now thinking the cleanest universal fix is a lightweight build-id endpoint — baking BUILD_TIME into both server and client bundles via Next's env config so the client can compare its own build id against the server's and detect a stale deploy that way.

I'll poll this every 60s and also check on visibilitychange, showing a reload banner when they differ and auto-reloading if no compose is open and the tab is idle. I'm figuring out how to compile DB filter rules into a managed Sieve script per mailbox, pushed through the existing filter API, including actions like moving to folders, flagging as seen, or redirecting for forwarding -- and I need to work out loop protection for forwards since Sieve's redirect doesn't easily support custom headers without an editheader extension, so I'm considering simpler safeguards like blocking forwards to the mailbox's own address.

The repro script reuses tokens.json from the scratch copy, which points to the same database, so that's fine. Now I'm ready to start coding, and I want to lay out the architecture concretely, starting with a client-side mail module that mirrors the server action signatures (listFolders, listMessages, getMessage, unread counts) but routes calls through a POST endpoint to a mail RPC handler.

That handler dispatches to an allowlist of operations pulled from the existing mail actions — things like setFlag, moveMessage, deleteMessage, markSpam, blockSender, and mailbox listing for both customer and admin contexts — while leaving sendMessage to go through the compose provider's own server action. I'm thinking through error handling (returning structured JSON with status codes, translating auth failures into a friendly session-expired message) and now I'm considering CSRF implications, since a lax same-site cookie won't be sent on certain cross-site POSTs, which affects how auth works for this route.

For build-version detection, I'm planning a response header that carries the build timestamp so the client can compare it against its own inlined build time and prompt a reload banner if they diverge — mail itself keeps working on stale tabs since rpc calls aren't tied to action IDs, but compose send via server action would break on a stale tab, so I'm weighing whether to route sending through rpc as well to avoid that issue.

On the server side, I'm also planning to rewrite cid: image references in message bodies into data URIs for inline attachments (with a size cap), since CSP allows data: images, and to eliminate the redundant double connection where both client and server mark messages as seen separately.

For listMessages, I'll add an optional keywords field to the summary type for label support. For unread counts, I'm sketching a function that queries STATUS on each accessible company mailbox with unseen/messages/uidNext and a short TTL cache, exposed through the unread API route scoped to company.

I'll check whether the admin inbox-unread endpoint already loops per mailbox and have it reuse this cached function instead. I'm also planning a MailUserPref model for storing last mailbox and notification preference, plus RPC ops for reading and updating it, and folder operations for creating, renaming, and deleting folders through the shared mail actions.

For deletion, I need to require explicit confirmation when a folder isn't empty since Dovecot will also delete the messages inside it, so the UI should prompt and the server should accept a confirm flag for non-empty folders. I'm also sketching out bulk action operations for flagging, moving, deleting, and marking spam across multiple UIDs using imapflow's UID set syntax, and starting to think through the filter system's rule types and whether zod is available for validation.

Now I'm working out the filter architecture — compiling to sieve, evaluating matches in TypeScript, handling presets, and syncing rules to Mailcow alongside the blocklist. I'm deciding that authorization should go through resolveMailbox so it works for both company and customer mailboxes later, with audit logging, even though the UI currently only exposes this to admins.

Writing Prisma schema fields...

I'm also weighing whether to merge blocked senders into a single MailFilterSender table rather than keeping separate blocklist logic, since the existing customer blockSender feature only stores entries in a sieve marker — when syncing a mailbox's postfilter, I'd need to combine the DB-stored block rules with that legacy marker data.

To preserve backward compatibility, I'd import the legacy marker list into the DB on first sync, then route all future blockSender calls through the same DB-backed path, generating a compiled script that's functionally identical to the old output when there are no other rules or allowlist entries. This keeps the new system elegant but does mean the simple customer-facing path now triggers DB writes, which I need to think through the implications of.

For the compiled script, I'm keeping the same description constant that marks it as the managed Nxeon filter so existing detection logic for "only one active filter" still works, rather than introducing a new label that would require dual-checking.

I'm structuring the generated sieve script: a header comment identifying it as Nxeon-managed with a backward-compatible address list, a conditional require statement for only the extensions actually used, and an allowlist block that stops processing early so allowed senders always land in the inbox.

But I realize Mailcow's global pre-filter already runs Rspamd and files spam into Junk before my postfilter even executes, so an allowlist here can't rescue messages already moved -- if that global script does a fileinto without a stop, my allowlist trying to fileinto INBOX would just duplicate the message rather than override the Junk placement. I need to document that the allowlist only protects against rules in my own postfilter, not against the global spam filing.

I'm sketching out the sieve rule structure instead: each rule checks sender address or domain and subject conditions, then accumulates flags like $NxFiltered and a rule-specific tag, optionally marks as read, applies a label, forwards a copy, files into a target folder (Inbox, Archive, Junk, or Trash depending on the action), and stops processing. I'm noting that imap4flags addflag calls modify an internal flag variable that subsequent fileinto/keep commands pick up, and these flags accumulate across multiple matching rules rather than resetting.

I'm now working out how to compile each condition type into sieve syntax -- matching sender address (exact, contains, starts/ends with), matching domain including subdomains, matching recipient (to/cc), matching subject or arbitrary header content, checking for header existence, and matching body text.

I'm also noting negation (notContains uses a "not" wrapper), that the default case-insensitive comparator works fine for ASCII, and that header names and folder paths need validation against character restrictions and length limits, with special characters like `*` and `?` escaped for :matches patterns. I also need to make sure the generated sieve only uses extensions the mail server's validator recognizes, like imap4flags and body.

For the "apply now" / test path, I'm planning to evaluate conditions against actual message headers and the first 64KB of body text identically to how sieve would, then map actions to IMAP operations—moving messages, flagging as read, applying labels—so the live apply-now behavior matches what the stored sieve rule would eventually do.

Forwarding is skipped during apply-now since it would send a real email; I'll mark it with a note instead. For the review queue, I need to search Junk, Trash, Archive and custom target folders for the $NxFiltered keyword over the past 30 days, and build a restore flow that moves the message back to INBOX using the UIDPLUS COPYUID mapping imapflow returns, then strips the flag — I should also check whether Hoodiecrow's test server actually supports arbitrary keyword flags via PERMANENTFLAGS.

Now I'm drafting the preset filter rules: DMARC and Search Console reports route to dedicated report folders and get marked read, review-solicitation and cold-outreach spam patterns route to spam or a cold-pitches folder, and I'm continuing to define keyword matches for SEO spam detection.

I need to watch for false positives, like a real Trustpilot business email getting caught by the review-sellers filter, since these presets are opt-in and should show a preview of matches before activation. I'm also thinking through forward loop protection, making sure the forwarding target is a valid external address and not the mailbox itself.

I also want to verify that if a mailbox forwards back to its source, even transitively, the system rejects it, capping each mailbox at three forward targets and leaning on Pigeonhole's built-in duplicate/loop safeguards alongside an auto-replied guard.

For the admin UI, I'm mapping out new pages under app/admin/mail — inbox, deliverability, mailboxes, templates, and filters — while setting up redirects from the old routes so query params are preserved, and considering optional shared MailClient props for features like per-mailbox unread counts and notifications.

I'm also thinking through refactoring MailClient's state to track the current view (address plus folder) and tag list responses with their originating view so stale results get ignored, using request-id counters for list and message fetches and a switching state to show a skeleton while changing mailboxes.

On failure to open a mailbox, I want to keep the old one active and show an error banner with retry, rather than disrupting the UI. List and message errors should show inline error panels with retry buttons instead of transient toasts, and refresh should re-query folders and messages while showing an "Updated" timestamp.

I'm also fixing the polling guard to use refs, adding periodic admin unread-count polling, and detecting new inbox mail via uidNext to trigger notifications. For bulk actions, I'm planning row checkboxes, select-all, a bulk toolbar with mark read/unread/star/archive/move/delete/spam, and keyboard shortcuts like x to select and shift+i/u for read state.

I'm also sketching the mailbox switcher with gradient initial avatars and unread badges, a toast system with longer red-toned error toasts that support retry/undo actions, and reading pane additions like "Filter like this," sender/domain blocking, error retry states, and an unread toggle — keeping customer-facing MailClient changes optional.

I'm thinking a from-only search would be lighter for the related-messages case, so I want to add an optional parameter to narrow the search fields instead of always searching all four.

Now I'm moving to the bigger piece: redesigning MailClient. I'm sketching new optional props for customer/company variants, a filters link override, initial unread counts, server-side mailbox memory, and notification state, along with the component's internal state for active address, folders, selected folder, message list, list metadata, loading/error states, and switch-in-progress tracking.

I'm using refs to track the current view (address, folder key, page, query) and separate request counters for list and message fetches so stale responses get ignored. I'm writing the loadList function that bumps the request counter, updates the view ref synchronously, fetches messages, and only applies results if the request is still current -- with polling using its own staleness check against both the request counter and the view ref.

Still writing switchMailbox...

Finishing the fetch logic to load the full message and populate error/loading states, passing error and retry handlers down to ReadingPane. I'm making sure all message operations use the list's committed address rather than the active one to avoid mismatches, and planning a polling mechanism for unread counts across mailboxes every 30 seconds plus on focus, with per-mailbox display in the switcher and a combined count reflected in the document title.

I also want to trigger browser notifications when uidNext increases for a mailbox and the tab is hidden, showing a generic "N new messages" message since fetching the subject isn't worth it, and refresh the inbox list if the active mailbox gets new mail while viewing page one with no search active. For scope control, I'll limit unread polling to the company variant for now rather than enabling it broadly for customer accounts, to avoid regressing existing behavior there.

For bulk actions, I'm planning row checkboxes that appear on hover, when any row is selected, or always on touch devices, plus a header "select all" checkbox. When selection is active, the tabs row gets replaced with a bulk action toolbar offering mark read/unread, star, archive, spam, delete, move, and clear, all using optimistic updates that fall back to a full reload on error. I also want keyboard shortcuts like x to toggle selection, Shift+I/U for read/unread, and u to return to the list view, which means updating the shortcut help panel accordingly.

For folder management, I'm adding a "+ New folder" button and per-folder rename/delete menus for company accounts, building a small modal dialog component rather than relying on ugly browser prompts. I'm also wiring up filter-from-message functionality so the reading pane can trigger navigation to a filters page prefilled with mailbox, sender, and subject, and starting to think about how mailbox avatars should look in the switcher.

For mailbox avatars, I'm leaning toward showing the brand mark for company mailboxes with initials as fallback, planning to verify the logo asset path later. I'm also expanding the toast system to support tone and action, adding a stale-build banner that listens for an update event and prompts the user to reload, and setting up a refresh mechanism that reloads the list and folders with an "Updated hh:mm" timestamp.

I'm confirming that search should work server-side across sender, recipient, subject, and body, with Esc clearing it, and checking that mobile layout and bulk toolbar handle wrapping fine. I traced the "stale Sent" concern back to a UI tab staleness issue rather than an actual data problem, since the direct check confirmed today's sends are present, and now I'm looking at how the refresh button should also trigger mailbox quota lookups via the Mailcow API for company mailboxes.

I'll keep the polling intervals as they are—45s for the list, 30s for unread counts—and drop the transition-based loading state in favor of an explicit one. Now I'm planning the full rewrite of the MailClient component, making sure to preserve deep-linking behavior, localStorage-based mailbox restoration with server preference as priority and localStorage as fallback, and leaving signature loading and mail settings untouched.

content.thinking:
I'm spotting a hydration mismatch: the UpdatedAgo component initializes its timestamp with Date.now() inside useState, so the server-computed value and the client's re-run on hydration differ slightly — the displayed "updated just now" text may match, but the title attribute using toLocaleString will differ since server and client time zones aren't guaranteed to align.

To fix this, I'll initialize `updatedAt` to 0 and set the real timestamp only inside a mount effect, having UpdatedAgo render nothing until that value is set.

content.content:
## Nxeon Mail — the native webmail client

**What it does.** A full IMAP/SMTP webmail client built into the customer portal, themed to match the
rest of the product. It replaced SOGo's own UI. Plus a CalDAV calendar and tasks view.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ alice@example.com ▾ │  Inbox  🔍 [               ]        [ ✎ Compose ]      │
├──────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
│ 📥 Inbox  12 │ ● Stripe        Payment recei… │  Payment receipt — INV-00042  │
│ 📤 Sent      │   2026-07-24 14:02            │  Stripe <no-reply@stripe.com>  │
│ 📝 Drafts    │ ○ Nick          Re: migration │  to me · 2026-07-24 14:02      │
│ 🗑 Trash     │   2026-07-24 11:40   📎2      │  ───────────────────────────   │
│ 🚫 Junk      │ ○ Cloudflare    Zone updated  │  Your payment of $195.58 has   │
│ 📁 Archive   │   2026-07-23 09:15            │  been received…                │
│              │                               │                                │
│              │            ▲ 50/page          │  📎 invoice.pdf   📎 logo.png  │
│              │                               │  [Reply] [Fwd] [Move ▾] [🗑]   │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
```

The mail and calendar routes render **full-bleed** — `components/portal/Shell.tsx:225` sets
`fullBleed` for them and `:507` swaps the padded main for `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden`.

**Transport.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/types.ts:8-11` — `MAIL_IMAP_HOST` defaults to `10.20.0.10` port
993, `MAIL_SMTP_HOST` the same host port 587. Neither variable is set in `.env`, so **those literals
are live**: the client talks to the Mailcow VM over the NAT bridge by IP, while sending the correct
TLS SNI (`MAIL_TLS_SERVERNAME`, default `mail.nxeon.cloud`, `lib/mail/imap.ts:70`) and **not**
verifying the certificate (`rejectUnauthorized: false`, `:309`). Same shape for SMTP
(`lib/actions-mail.ts:490-497`). Connections are per-request and always closed — `withImap` (`:320`),
`withMailbox` (`:342`).

**Credentials.** `Mailbox.passwordEnc` (`prisma/schema.prisma:675`), AES-256-GCM via
`lib/crypto-box.ts:22` with a key derived by `scryptSync(AUTH_SECRET, "nxeon-byok", 32)`. Every mail
operation resolves through `resolveMailbox` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:244`): `requireUser()` at `:245`, only
mailboxes where `subscription.userId === user.id` (`:247`), and an explicitly requested address must
match one of them or it throws (`:270`).

**`Mailbox.address` is now `@unique` globally** (`prisma/schema.prisma:674`), with the schema comment
naming the cross-tenant takeover it closes — see the Business email chapter.

**What works.**

| Feature | Where |
|---|---|
| Folder list with roles and counts | `lib/actions-mail.ts:102`; `folderRole` `lib/mail/imap.ts:360` (SPECIAL-USE first, then name heuristics) |
| Message list, 50/page, IMAP SEARCH over subject/from/to/body | `lib/actions-mail.ts:153`, `:167` |
| Read, HTML sanitised, `\Seen` best-effort | `:229`, `safeHtml` `lib/mail/render.ts:25` |
| Flags, move, delete (→ Trash, then expunge) | `:521`, `:567` |
| Compose with attachments, ≤10 files / 20 MB | `:411`; caps `:318`; decode+validate `:355` |
| Attachment download by `<uid>:<part>` | `app/api/mail/attachment/route.ts:14` |
| Identity on outgoing mail — display name → `From`, `replyTo` → `Reply-To`, `organization` → header | `lib/actions-mail.ts:468-487` |
| Sent copy is byte-identical to what was sent (compiled once via `streamTransport`) | `:473-488` |
| Rich signature with image upload and size presets | `components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx:297`, `:655`, `:688` |
| Auto-reply and forwarding as **real Mailcow sieve** | `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:298`, `:388`, `:448`; compiler `lib/mail/sieve.ts` |
| Aliases (real Mailcow) | `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:522` |
| Mailbox password reveal + reset | `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:744`, `:776` |
| Orphan-mailbox adoption from Mailcow | `lib/mail/imap.ts:126` `discoverMailboxes` |
| CalDAV calendar + tasks | `lib/calendar/caldav.ts:51`, actions `lib/actions-calendar.ts:159` |

Sieve is worth a note: `lib/mail/sieve.ts` compiles **one managed script** (rationale at `:22`) with
markers (`:55`) so `getMailRuleStatus` (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:361`) derives status from the
**live script**, not from the DB. Rules are pushed to Mailcow *before* the DB write (`:416`), so the DB
can never claim a rule that the mail server does not have. `assertRulesAllowed` (`:336`) refuses
unverified external domains.

**What is missing.** No folder create/rename/delete anywhere. No draft saving — the only IMAP `append`
is the Sent copy (`lib/actions-mail.ts:504`).

**Honest note — the signature is appended in the browser.** `sendMessage` never touches it;
`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx:165-186` does, fed by
`components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx:124`. And `app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx:34` passes only the
legacy plain-text `signature` as `initialSignature`. So a signature set in the rich editor may not
appear on mail composed through a path that does not run that client-side append.

```

```

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|
| `2d8fedd` | Game servers renew at their game-plan price, not the base VPS plan | **Real.** `renewalQuote` delegates to `renewalCharge` and owns no arithmetic; a test asserts the file contains none. The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |
| `f28f15e` | Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt | **Real.** `packMetadata` throws before `checkout.sessions.create`; the sold price rides in metadata; the receipt attaches an invoice or points at billing history, never promises one it does not send |
| `3aa24d7` | Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF) | **Mixed by design.** The two auth lockouts and the NAT flush are genuinely fixed. Email verification is **complete and deliberately disarmed** — `email_verification_enforced` defaults to `false` because the platform's DKIM record is missing (gaps 1 and 9). Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |
| `7490131` | Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI | **Real.** Three launch blockers from `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, all reproduced in a browser and all byte-identical in production, plus the card-save UI that had been wrongly marked complete |
| `156b6ac` | Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run | **Real, and verified on the live queue** rather than asserted: jobs drain, the permanent path settles, notifications stopped climbing |
| `4ea9790` | Promo-basis proration, post-cutover TLS, 8 more migration defects | **Real.** `Server.termPromoPercent` makes the proration round trip net zero by construction; the TLS pass stopped being dead code; 4 rows backfilled from real billing records with 0 fallbacks |
| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

The through-line across all seven is the defect this codebase keeps producing in new places: **a second
definition of something that already had one.** A second renewal formula. A second promo basis. A
second place `lastAutoBackup` could be written. A second email-normalisation. The fix, every time, was
to delete the duplicate rather than to make the two agree.

## Session log — 2026-07-27 (evening: portal UX, mail, ops fixes)
the panel's Files feature timed out, and firewall sync retried 3× and failed to authenticate — both
against a server the customer insisted had a working, reachable management key.

- **Root cause, fully verified before touching anything**: `connectionTarget()` (`lib/sftp.ts`) has
  always hardcoded port 22 for ANY server with a dedicated IP, ignoring `Server.sshPort` entirely for
  that branch (that field is the NAT-mapped *external* port for non-dedicated servers — a different,
  `@unique` concept, not safe to reuse here). `nc -zv <ip> 22` timed out; `nc -zv <ip> 2222` succeeded;
  connecting directly with the server's own stored management key on `:2222` worked immediately
  (`sshd -T` confirmed `port 2222`). So the management key and the connection plumbing were both fine
  — the platform was just always dialing the wrong port for this one server.
- **Fix**: new nullable `Server.guestSshPort` column (additive, `db push`'d — changes nothing for any
  existing server, since `null` falls back to `?? 22`, today's exact behavior). `connectionTarget()`'s
  dedicated-IP branch now reads `server.guestSshPort ?? 22` instead of a bare `22`. Selected into
  `lib/actions-files.ts`'s server query (the Files feature); `worker/firewall.ts` already `include`s
  the whole row so it picked it up for free. New unit tests in `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`
  pin both the override and the (unchanged) default. Admin server detail page now shows "Guest SSH
  port override" for any server with a dedicated IP, so this doesn't stay a hidden DB-only field.
- **The firewall side needed a second, separate finding**: even with the port fixed, `syncFirewall`
  would still fail — this guest's `iptables` (legacy) returns "Incompatible with this kernel" (likely
  1Panel's own nftables-only setup). Checked the LIVE guest directly: `iptables -L INPUT` showed only
  UFW's own chains (`ufw-before-input` etc.), policy DROP — confirming the platform's `NXEON_FW` chain
  has in fact never once been successfully applied to this guest, so there was nothing live to
  "detach". The customer's 6 stale `FirewallRule` DB rows are display-only leftovers; deleting them
  requires no guest-side sync (and syncing them now would risk appending a default-DROP that doesn't
  know about port 2222 — `FW_KEEP_OPEN_TCP_PORTS` only keeps 22 open — so deliberately did NOT trigger
  a sync). `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs are only ever created by `lib/actions-firewall.ts` on an explicit rule
  edit (confirmed — no periodic/cron trigger exists), so once those 6 rows are gone, nothing re-fires
  on its own.
- **Not yet done**: deleting the 6 stale `FirewallRule` rows was blocked by the auto-mode permission
  classifier ("Modify Shared Resources") on a direct DB write — needs the owner to run it or grant it.
  Worth a platform-wide follow-up too: any guest running an nftables-only setup (1Panel defaults to
  this) can never successfully use the panel firewall feature at all, independent of this port issue.

**Files:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`.
