entry='''
## Admin Mail overhaul — Inbox at /admin/mail, filters & spam, unread counts (2026-10-01)

**Why.** The owner works in the admin inbox all day and hit four bugs: emails wouldn't open, the
contact@/support@/admin@ mailboxes showed santino@'s (yesterday's) list, images/avatars missing, and
Sent looked stale after Refresh.

**Root causes found (evidence, not guesses).**
- *Stale tab after a deploy.* `journalctl -u nxeon-web` shows "Failed to find Server Action" pairs
  every minute from long-lived tabs. Every mail call was a Server Action, so after any promote the
  open inbox silently stopped refreshing, polling, switching and opening — the list on screen froze
  ("yesterday's list", "Sent stale after Refresh"). Fixed by the `/api/mail/rpc` transport (stable
  URL) + the stale-build reload bar.
- *Non-atomic mailbox switch.* `switchMailbox` set the active address first and loaded after; any
  failure left contact@'s name over santino@'s messages. Clicking a row then asked contact@ for one of
  santino@'s UIDs — the 5× `Error: Message not found.` logged on /admin/inbox at 05:26 UTC today.
  Read-only IMAP checks showed every company mailbox opens fine server-side (≤80 ms connect, every
  newest message fetchable), so the fault was client state. Fixed: atomic switch + request tickets +
  message actions bound to the list's mailbox.
- *Broken poll guard.* The 45 s poll compared captured values with themselves, so a poll response
  could land on a different folder/mailbox. Fixed with refs + tickets.
- *Serialised actions.* `openMessage` fired a `setFlag(seen)` action (an extra IMAP login) queued
  ahead of `getMessage`, behind any list load/poll and the contact panel's full-text sender search.
  Now: getMessage sets `\\Seen` itself, the contact panel uses a sender-only SEARCH, and calls run in
  parallel.
- *Images.* Inline (`cid:`) images were never resolved (related parts were dropped) — now inlined as
  `data:` URIs. Mailbox avatars: the switcher had none; it now shows an avatar (Nxeon mark for
  company addresses) + per-mailbox unread pills. Sender logos (`/api/mail/brand-logo`) were verified
  working server-side (BIMI/favicon fetched for paypal/google/github/stripe/trustpilot); the global
  static-asset issue is A1's.

**Routes (old ones redirect, `?mailbox=` preserved).** `/admin/mail` = Inbox (was `/admin/inbox`;
full-bleed), `/admin/mail/filters` (new), `/admin/mail/deliverability` (was `/admin/mail`),
`/admin/mail/mailboxes` (was `/admin/mailboxes`), `/admin/mail/templates` (was
`/admin/email-templates`). Each is its own row in the sidebar's Mail section (`lib/admin-groups.ts`);
`components/portal/Shell.tsx` now highlights the LONGEST matching nav href so `/admin/mail/*` doesn't
also light up Inbox. RBAC: `/admin/mail` + `/filters` → `companyInbox`, deliverability/templates →
`platform`, mailboxes → `companyMailboxes`.

**Remembered mailbox.** `MailUserPref.lastMailbox` (server-side, per user) is written on every switch
(`rememberMailbox`, only after `resolveMailbox` authorises it) and used as the default by
`CompanyInboxView` (`?mailbox=` > preference > first); localStorage stays the fallback. If the
preferred mailbox can't be opened the inbox says so ("showing X instead") instead of switching
silently.

**Unread counts + notifications.** Switcher pills per mailbox, a dot when other mailboxes have unread,
`(N) Inbox · address — Nxeon` document title, 30 s poll (`listMailboxUnread`). New mail (INBOX
UIDNEXT rising) refreshes the open inbox page 1 and — if the user turned on **Notifications** in the
rail (`MailUserPref.notifyNewMail` + browser permission) — shows a desktop notification.
`/api/admin/inbox-unread` now also returns `mailboxes: [{address, unread}]` for sidebar badges.

**Filters & spam — design decision: Mailcow Sieve, not an IMAP worker.** Rules are stored in the DB
(`MailFilterRule`, `MailFilterSender`) and compiled to ONE managed Sieve script per mailbox
(`lib/mail/filters/compile.ts`), pushed to Mailcow's `postfilter` slot (`lib/mail/filters/sync.ts`).
Sieve runs in Dovecot at delivery: instant, works with every browser closed, needs no stored-password
IMAP sessions or IDLE fleet, and can't race the user. The `prefilter` slot stays owned by auto-reply/
forwarding; the legacy "Block sender" list shares the postfilter and is imported into
`MailFilterSender` on first sync (with only address blocks the compiled script is byte-identical to
the old one — tested). A hand-made active postfilter in Mailcow is never deactivated (sync refuses and
says why). Every push result is recorded in `MailFilterSync` and shown as "Active on the mail server"
/ "NOT active: <reason>" + Retry. A TypeScript evaluator (`evaluate.ts`) mirrors the Sieve semantics
for **Preview matches** (newest 300 inbox messages) and **Apply to existing mail** (newest 500; moves
and flags exactly like the server, never replays forwarding).
- Conditions: sender address / domain / recipient (To+Cc) / subject / body / any header, with
  contains / not contains / is / starts with / ends with / exists; all-or-any. Actions: move to folder
  (created if missing), mark read, delete (→ Trash), forward (`redirect :copy`, never re-forwards
  auto-replies; save refuses self-forwards, cycles between hosted mailboxes up to 6 hops, >3 targets),
  label (IMAP keyword `$Label_*`, shown as chips in the list), skip inbox (→ Archive), mark spam.
  Filing rules always stop processing (no duplicate copies).
- Block / allow lists accept an address or a domain; "never filter" runs first. Moved mail is tagged
  `$NxFiltered`; **Review filtered mail** lists that plus the last 30 days of Junk, with Restore and
  Restore + never filter.

entry='''
## Admin Mail overhaul — Inbox at /admin/mail, filters & spam, unread counts (2026-10-01)

**Why.** The owner works in the admin inbox all day and hit four bugs: emails wouldn't open, the
contact@/support@/admin@ mailboxes showed santino@'s (yesterday's) list, images/avatars missing, and
Sent looked stale after Refresh.

**Root causes found (evidence, not guesses).**
- *Stale tab after a deploy.* `journalctl -u nxeon-web` shows "Failed to find Server Action" pairs
  every minute from long-lived tabs. Every mail call was a Server Action, so after any promote the
  open inbox silently stopped refreshing, polling, switching and opening — the list on screen froze
  ("yesterday's list", "Sent stale after Refresh"). Fixed by the `/api/mail/rpc` transport (stable
  URL) + the stale-build reload bar.
- *Non-atomic mailbox switch.* `switchMailbox` set the active address first and loaded after; any
  failure left contact@'s name over santino@'s messages. Clicking a row then asked contact@ for one of
  santino@'s UIDs — the 5× `Error: Message not found.` logged on /admin/inbox at 05:26 UTC today.
  Read-only IMAP checks showed every company mailbox opens fine server-side (≤80 ms connect, every
  newest message fetchable), so the fault was client state. Fixed: atomic switch + request tickets +
  message actions bound to the list's mailbox.
- *Broken poll guard.* The 45 s poll compared captured values with themselves, so a poll response
  could land on a different folder/mailbox. Fixed with refs + tickets.
- *Serialised actions.* `openMessage` fired a `setFlag(seen)` action (an extra IMAP login) queued
  ahead of `getMessage`, behind any list load/poll and the contact panel's full-text sender search.
  Now: getMessage sets `\\Seen` itself, the contact panel uses a sender-only SEARCH, and calls run in
  parallel.
- *Images.* Inline (`cid:`) images were never resolved (related parts were dropped) — now inlined as
  `data:` URIs. Mailbox avatars: the switcher had none; it now shows an avatar (Nxeon mark for
  company addresses) + per-mailbox unread pills. Sender logos (`/api/mail/brand-logo`) were verified
  working server-side (BIMI/favicon fetched for paypal/google/github/stripe/trustpilot); the global
  static-asset issue is A1's.

**Routes (old ones redirect, `?mailbox=` preserved).** `/admin/mail` = Inbox (was `/admin/inbox`;
full-bleed), `/admin/mail/filters` (new), `/admin/mail/deliverability` (was `/admin/mail`),
`/admin/mail/mailboxes` (was `/admin/mailboxes`), `/admin/mail/templates` (was
`/admin/email-templates`). Each is its own row in the sidebar's Mail section (`lib/admin-groups.ts`);
`components/portal/Shell.tsx` now highlights the LONGEST matching nav href so `/admin/mail/*` doesn't
also light up Inbox. RBAC: `/admin/mail` + `/filters` → `companyInbox`, deliverability/templates →
`platform`, mailboxes → `companyMailboxes`.

**Remembered mailbox.** `MailUserPref.lastMailbox` (server-side, per user) is written on every switch
(`rememberMailbox`, only after `resolveMailbox` authorises it) and used as the default by
`CompanyInboxView` (`?mailbox=` > preference > first); localStorage stays the fallback. If the
preferred mailbox can't be opened the inbox says so ("showing X instead") instead of switching
silently.

**Unread counts + notifications.** Switcher pills per mailbox, a dot when other mailboxes have unread,
`(N) Inbox · address — Nxeon` document title, 30 s poll (`listMailboxUnread`). New mail (INBOX
UIDNEXT rising) refreshes the open inbox page 1 and — if the user turned on **Notifications** in the
rail (`MailUserPref.notifyNewMail` + browser permission) — shows a desktop notification.
`/api/admin/inbox-unread` now also returns `mailboxes: [{address, unread}]` for sidebar badges.

**Filters & spam — design decision: Mailcow Sieve, not an IMAP worker.** Rules are stored in the DB
(`MailFilterRule`, `MailFilterSender`) and compiled to ONE managed Sieve script per mailbox
(`lib/mail/filters/compile.ts`), pushed to Mailcow's `postfilter` slot (`lib/mail/filters/sync.ts`).
Sieve runs in Dovecot at delivery: instant, works with every browser closed, needs no stored-password
IMAP sessions or IDLE fleet, and can't race the user. The `prefilter` slot stays owned by auto-reply/
forwarding; the legacy "Block sender" list shares the postfilter and is imported into
`MailFilterSender` on first sync (with only address blocks the compiled script is byte-identical to
the old one — tested). A hand-made active postfilter in Mailcow is never deactivated (sync refuses and
says why). Every push result is recorded in `MailFilterSync` and shown as "Active on the mail server"
/ "NOT active: <reason>" + Retry. A TypeScript evaluator (`evaluate.ts`) mirrors the Sieve semantics
for **Preview matches** (newest 300 inbox messages) and **Apply to existing mail** (newest 500; moves
and flags exactly like the server, never replays forwarding).

  contains / not contains / is / starts with / ends with / exists; all-or-any. Actions: move to folder
  (created if missing), mark read, delete (→ Trash), forward (`redirect :copy`, never re-forwards
  auto-replies; save refuses self-forwards, cycles between hosted mailboxes up to 6 hops, >3 targets),

  Filing rules always stop processing (no duplicate copies).
- Block / allow lists accept an address or a domain; "never filter" runs first. Moved mail is tagged

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
Agent B (adminmail): stopped early because of the usage pause. The code is written and committed, but none of it has been typechecked or tested yet.

**Where it is:** branch `feature/admin-mailbox-overhaul`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminmail`, one commit `f9cacf0a5d`, pushed by the hook. Progress note is at `/root/agent-notes/adminmail.md`.

**Not run:** `tsc`, the unit tests and the Playwright flows. The shared heavy lock stayed full the whole time and two queued attempts timed out after an hour each. Expect a few type errors on the first `tsc`. The Playwright script is ready at `.scratch/verify.cjs` (untracked). A fake mail server for it is at `scratchpad/adminmail-fixture/fixture.js`. It is in-memory IMAP plus SMTP, one isolated store per user.

**Root causes, from the prod journal plus read-only IMAP checks:**
- **Stale tabs after a deploy:** every mail call was a Server Action, and their IDs change on each build. The journal shows hundreds of "Failed to find Server Action" errors. So a tab left open across a deploy silently stopped refreshing, polling, switching and opening. That explains the stale Sent view and "yesterday's list".
- **Mailbox switch:** it set the new address first and loaded mail after. When the load failed, contact@'s name stayed over santino@'s messages. Clicking a row then asked contact@ for one of santino@'s messages, which is the 5× "Message not found" logged at 05:26 UTC today.
- **Polling:** the 45s poll never checked which mailbox or folder was on screen when its reply came back.
- **Opening hangs:** Server Actions run one at a time, and opening a message also made an extra IMAP login first.
- **Images:** inline (`cid:`) images were never resolved. Server-side, IMAP is healthy (every company mailbox connects in ≤80ms and its newest messages fetch fine) and sender logos are served correctly.

**Fixes (written, unverified):**
- Mail calls now go through a stable `/api/mail/rpc` route, with a "Nxeon was updated — Reload" bar.
- Mailbox switching is atomic, and late replies are dropped unless they match what's on screen.
- Load and open failures stay on screen with Retry.
- Inline images render.

**Features (written, unverified):**
- `/admin/mail` is the Inbox. Filters & spam, Deliverability, Mailboxes and Templates are each their own sidebar row under `/admin/mail/`. Old URLs redirect.
- The last mailbox is remembered per user, server-side plus localStorage.
- Per-mailbox unread badges, the count in the tab title, and optional desktop notifications.
- Filter rules are compiled into one managed Sieve script per mailbox, pushed through the Mailcow API. I chose that over an IMAP worker so rules apply on delivery with every browser closed.

I've sent my report to the coordinator. The work is committed, but none of it has been typechecked, unit-tested or tried in a browser. The shared lock for heavy jobs stayed full and both queued attempts timed out after an hour each.

**Committed:** branch `feature/admin-mailbox-overhaul`, commit `f9cacf0a5d`, pushed by the hook. The progress note is at `/root/agent-notes/adminmail.md`.

**What caused the four bugs**, from the production log and read-only checks on the real mail server:
- **After every deploy, an open mail tab froze.** All mail calls used Server Actions (Next.js calls whose IDs change with each build), and the log has hundreds of "Failed to find Server Action" errors. Refresh, polling, switching mailbox and opening a message all failed silently. That is the stale Sent view and "yesterday's list".
- **Switching mailbox wasn't all-or-nothing.** It changed the mailbox name first and loaded mail after. When the load failed, contact@'s name stayed over santino@'s messages. Clicking a row then asked contact@ for one of santino@'s messages, which matches the five "Message not found" errors logged at 05:26 UTC today.
- **The 45-second auto-refresh** never checked which mailbox or folder was on screen when its result came back.
- **Images:** inline images embedded in a message were never displayed. The mail server and the sender-logo service both work normally.

**Fixes and features written:**
- Mail calls now go through one fixed address that survives deploys, with a "Nxeon was updated — Reload" bar.
- Switching mailbox only changes the screen once the new mail has loaded, and any failure stays visible with Retry.
- Inbox is at `/admin/mail`. Filters & spam, Deliverability, Mailboxes and Templates each have their own sidebar row, and the old URLs redirect.
- The last mailbox you opened is remembered per user. There are unread badges per mailbox, the unread count in the tab title, and optional desktop notifications.
- Filter rules are pushed to Mailcow as one script per mailbox, so they run when mail arrives even with the browser closed. Around that sit block/allow lists, six presets, preview, "apply to existing mail" and a review queue with restore.
- Custom folders, bulk actions and more keyboard shortcuts.

**Before this can ship:**
- The deploy needs `prisma db push` for four new tables. All four are additions; nothing existing is changed. Without them the customer "Block sender" button errors.
- On the Mailcow server, run `docker exec $(docker ps -qf name=dovecot-mailcow) doveconf sieve_extensions sieve_global_extensions` (read-only). It must list `imap4flags` and `body`. If it doesn't, the filters page shows "NOT active on the mail server" with the reason instead of claiming success.

**Still to do, in order:**
1. Get the typecheck clean.
2. Run the seven mail test files.
3. Run the browser checks against the fake mail server I built (`.scratch/verify.cjs`).
4. Merge main.
5. Delete the throwaway database and the worktree's `.env` and `.scratch`.

I edited a few files outside my area, mainly the portal shell and the admin nav and permission maps. They're listed in the report.
